correctness.rationale: The positive-real-part branch is smooth and the derivative of the lift is (1-epsilon^2)/|1+epsilon exp(2 pi i x)|^2. The odd correction crosses level q at the stated p and r on either side of its unique maximum delta. Monotonicity in x and d gives the two common strip inclusions. For alpha=pi q set T=cos(alpha) and W=sqrt(epsilon^2-sin(alpha)^2). At the level-q roots, rotation by -alpha gives positive moduli T+W and T-W, respectively. Since (T+W)(T-W)=1-epsilon^2, the endpoint multipliers are (T-W)/(T+W) and its reciprocal, reproducing the arcosh formula. Monotonicity of the derivative in distance from 0 proves both lift Lipschitz bounds; d=q fixes both relevant endpoints and achieves the derivative bounds, also for iterates. Nested forward and inverse images of the strips give unique entire trajectories and only b_0 stays forever in J. Outside I and J a lift moves toward I, cannot cross back into J, and either enters I or approaches its endpoint: away from the endpoint and r the displacement is uniformly bounded below in magnitude. A slightly enlarged strip is contracting there, giving exponential convergence. Uniform limits of continuous pullback/forward approximants give the continuous graphs over the invertible cat base. Constant d=delta is parabolic; for q>delta choose delta<d<min(q,1/2). The expansion of T/sqrt(1-epsilon^2) about q=delta gives the stated square-root coefficient. At q=0 the stated number is the local fixed-point multiplier (inverse at the repeller); sharp Lipschitz comparisons on singleton strips are vacuous. The frozen checker gives finite diagnostics only; the infinite-time and sharp statements follow from the reviewed analytic proof.

value.rationale: Constant or periodic analysis need not guarantee contraction under switching. Explicit uniform barriers, an attained robustness margin/rate and an exact exceptional trajectory give a deterministic baseline for arbitrary forcing and an entire-torus basin criterion for the cat map.
